svg.title: Instruction binding: original and fresh extension
svg.desc: held-out maps, frozen pipeline, run after two interrupted attempts; not the pre-registered sealed claim. fresh held-out extension, run after the freeze; not the pre-registered sealed claim. Two earlier attempts on the same maps stopped early when our own frozen-code guard tripped. In the first, a test rewrote a pinned fixture; in the second, the engine wrote scratch files inside its pinned folder. No planning code changed. They completed 36 and 91 rows; both are published as they are and not pooled with the final run. Where the same rows ran again in the final run, attempt 1 matched the final run on 36 of the 38 rows it opened (status and lifts; 37 of 38 on verdict alone) and attempt 2 on 91 of 91, reported separately.

g.text: First plans that broke the rule only

svg.text: Exact two-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% intervals. Binding requires a same-map no-rule baseline that is a complete, fresh-audited L0 pass and fails
the intended-rule recheck; the rule and hash must match the instruction allocation.
The numerator requires a complete, obedient, fresh-audited instructed L0 pass. Already-obeyed and unavailable counterfactuals remain separate
(code15 binding-definition erratum).
In 3.1, on the other 6 of 24 voyages, the first plan already obeyed the rule, which proves nothing about instruction binding.
Confirmation here is exact expected-rule match against an answer key, not a human planner confirmation; these were templated sentences.
The 3.1 broader count, 18/24, is a different denominator; it is not the binding result. Passes require a full checker pass and completion.
3.1 uses frozen v3 (a11b4202…); ext-1 uses frozen v4 (acf2f275…), with byte-identical planning code.
Envelope: up to 195 boxes in a half-ship section of 500–800 TEU feeder ships, at most 70% of that section; empty section on arrival, one loading
call. Other bays hold fixed synthetic cargo.
Confirmation is exact expected-rule match, not a human planner confirmation. These are templated sentences.
SECONDARY pooling combines completed 3.1 and ext-1 envelope maps only; it is not one experiment. No tiny/small maps or interrupted attempts enter
the sum.
Same synthetic generator family, not new voyage types, independent replication, or recovery of a sealed claim.
Two earlier attempts on the same maps stopped early when our own frozen-code guard tripped. In the first, a test rewrote a pinned fixture; in the
second, the engine wrote scratch files inside its pinned folder. No planning code changed. They completed 36 and 91 rows; both are published as
they are and not pooled with the final run. Where the same rows ran again in the final run, attempt 1 matched the final run on 36 of the 38 rows
it opened (status and lifts; 37 of 38 on verdict alone) and attempt 2 on 91 of 91, reported separately.
Source: measurements/ext-1/FIGURES.json · recorded results only; no planning or checker rerun
